title: AES-GCM decrypt: oversized authTagSz silently skips SET_TAG ioctl
description: ~~CORRECTED from P0~~ The original concern was authentication bypass if SET_TAG ioctl is skipped. Both premises were wrong after checking the source of truth. (1) CRYPTO2DEV_TAG_MAXLEN = 16 (uapi/crypto2dev_ioctl.h:88). Standard AES-GCM tags are at most 16 bytes — authTagSz > CRYPTO2DEV_TAG_MAXLEN is unreachable from any standard call path. (2) The kernel driver (wolfssl_aes_gcm_finalize, line 484): if SET_TAG was never called, ctx->taglen == 0, and FINALIZE returns -EINVAL. The device fails closed — no silent authentication bypass. Remaining issue: the code is still inconsistent — AAD oversize returns BUFFER_E, tag oversize silently skips. This should return BUFFER_E for symmetry and defensive hygiene, but it is not a security hole. Reduce to P2 defensive hardening.
